title: Alpha007 folded reversal with kurtosis-skewness regime weighting
summary: Alpha007 research found that folding the signed volume-spike reversal signal and weighting it by kurtosis minus skewness improved decile monotonicity by identifying crash-regime conditions.

mechanism.payer: crowded or forced short-horizon traders who overreact to large price moves under abnormal volume
mechanism.receiver: liquidity provider or mean-reversion holder compensated when crash-regime overreaction fades
mechanism.random_object: folded absolute 7-day price move under volume condition, modulated by rolling return distribution shape
mechanism.math_forced_insight: Signed ts-rank and folded absolute move are not algebraically equivalent; the distribution-moment regime preserves crash-tail information while avoiding bubble-regime over-amplification.

evidence.boundary: Regime transform improved monotonicity but should still be checked for OOS and cost before being treated as standalone production alpha.
evidence.qlib_only_boundary: Controlled Qlib-only Alpha007 record is weak/negative and should not override the separate folded kurt-skew candidate mechanism; use it as a sign and portfolio-construction caution.

relations.note: Kurtosis and skewness classify crash/bubble distribution shape before weighting the folded signal.
Fold plus kurt-skew regime refines the original signed Alpha007 formula.
Testing showed ts_rank(delta) is not equivalent to ts_rank(abs(delta)) times sign.
Use rolling skewness/kurtosis when a factor's tail buckets fail in crash or bubble regimes.

reuse_guidance: Retrieve this node when a factor has tail-bucket instability, crash-regime failure, or signed-vs-magnitude ambiguity.
Use distribution moments to explain regime-specific payer behavior, not as decorative nonlinear weighting.
Treat improved monotonicity as useful but still require long-side and OOS/cost evidence.
